top_choice_rationale: P001 credits a specific, traceable pair: Katori for the magic-wavelength lattice and first strontium lattice clock, and Ye for taking it to the 1e-18 level with a fully measured systematics budget. The result is reproduced at several independent laboratories, and the concept is distinct from the 2005 comb and 2012 ion-control prizes. It is invention and measurement rather than a surprise from nature, and Lemonde, Takamoto and the ion-clock groups lie outside the pair, so the citation must stay narrow. Even so, it is the most mature and most cleanly allocated proposal on the slate. P002 is real, long-confirmed physics, but the three-name allocation leaves out Mele, Hasan and the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal, and it bundles quantum spin Hall and quantum anomalous Hall as one achievement, which I cannot judge as a non-specialist. I still prefer it to no award.
recusal_note: No conflict with Katori, Ye, Kane, Molenkamp or Xue apparent from profile. My PAMELA, Fermi-LAT and XL-Calibur memberships place me near the astroparticle community of the IceCube candidate, which is not on this slate.
